summary: Reviewed all 213 AI tool rows (idx 262-474) with about 70 web calls plus curl redirect checks. 57 high/medium data findings with URLs: 11 discontinued tools to remove (Botkeeper, Height, Socratic, Clockwise, Limitless, Rewind, Adept, Phind, Mentat, plus acquired-and-absorbed Zavvy and Pymetrics), more than 15 acquisitions or renames (Windsurf is now Devin Desktop; Searchie should be Searchspring/Athos; Dynamic Yield is Mastercard, not McDonald's; Kira, Casetext, Causal, Lacework, Wiz, Paradox), 6 wrong websites (Crush points to an unrelated blog, Jules to Firebase Studio, Copilot CLI is a 404), and stale prices (Ashby, Power BI, Klaviyo, Metabase, Grafana, MagicSchool, Elpass $299/mo against a real $19.99/yr, Kiro, Cody). 5 of the 33 surfaced rows need fixes (262, 264, 304, 361, 414). Logic: unsized directory listings bypass the size filter, so enterprise or off-target vendors fill 'More vendors' for small firms. aiForProblems' first-3 list order surfaces Enterprise SOC, recruiting and legal tools under a 'low-cost' label. URL hrefs are not scheme-validated (javascript: passes esc()).

logic.issue: moreVendors' size filter keeps every listing with no size (`!e.sz.length`), and the sort (Canadian first, then A-Z) puts these unsized Canadian listings in the six slots. The heading still says 'sized for your business'.
logic.scenario: Firm with fewer than 10 people (size xs). Accounting gets Caseware (audit software for accounting firms), FundThrough (invoice financing), Stax Bill and Versapay (enterprise AR). Plooto and Wave are the only items sized 's'. Cybersecurity gets Cybeats, Flare, Genetec (enterprise video surveillance), Plurilock and Security Compass, all unsized. ERP gets ACCEO and Cayenta (utility billing CIS). Field service gets Promise Robotics. Overall, 287 of 781 directory listings are unsized (37%), and 64 of the 136 surfaced rows are unsized.
logic.fix: In moreVendors, rank listings with a size match first. Show unsized listings only to fill remaining slots, labelled 'size not stated'. For xs/sm firms, exclude listings sized only 'l' or priced Enterprise. Backfill sz in the master lists.

logic.issue: Off-category listings in directory groups reach 'More vendors' (the CAT id is the only filter), and service firms or holding companies show up as software vendors.
logic.scenario: 'More field service vendors' shows Promise Robotics (robotic off-site construction). Accounting shows FundThrough (a lender). Backup and cybersecurity shows Genetec (physical security). Collaboration shows Firmex (data room). Practice management shows Dye & Durham (legal-software conglomerate). ERP lists Constellation Software (a holding company).
logic.fix: Data QA on the dir group for each listing. Add an entry type (software, service, holding) and filter out anything that isn't software in moreVendors.

logic.issue: Industry filtering works at group level only. grpFitsInd tests whether the whole category or group serves the industry, never the individual vendor, and moreVendors ignores ans.ind completely.
logic.scenario: Clinic owner: 'More accounting vendors' gives the same list as for a manufacturer (Caseware, Cayenta-style enterprise vendors). In the directory, picking an industry either keeps every listing in the group or hides the whole group.
logic.fix: Add inds per directory listing. Filter moreVendors and vdRows on e.inds where it is present, and fall back to group level otherwise.

logic.issue: The 'See all N in the Vendor Directory' count doesn't match what the directory shows. N is the size-filtered, unscored count, but vdGo resets vd.size to '' and the directory also lists scored items.
logic.scenario: Size xs, accounting: the button says 'See all 11', but the directory opens with 19 listings. ERP: 36 versus 81.
logic.fix: Pass the size to vdGo (map SZA[ans.size] to the directory size filter) or change the button text to 'See all accounting vendors'.

logic.issue: The Vendor Directory size filter (vdRows) also lets unsized listings through, and their Size cell is blank, so a user filtering 'Small' can't tell size-confirmed listings from unknown ones. vd.size is compared directly with e.sz codes (s/m/l) while the assessment uses xs/sm/md/lg, so the #vd-size option values must be s/m/l. The HTML wasn't provided, so this needs checking.
logic.scenario: Filter size = Small, category = Backup and cybersecurity: 1Password, BlackBerry and Absolute Software (sized 'l') are correctly hidden, but Genetec, Flare and Cybeats (unsized) appear alongside Rewind (sized 's') with nothing to tell them apart.
logic.fix: Render 'Not stated' in the Size cell and add a 'confirmed size only' toggle. Assert that the option values are s/m/l.

logic.issue: The mc loop takes the first category (quick win, then top priorities) that has any directory entries. If the quick-win category has none, the block silently switches to a different category from the 'Three options' list just above it. With ans.size unset, want=[], so only unsized listings can show.
logic.scenario: Quick win = a category with no directory rows (e.g., mrp: 0 rows). 'More vendors' then shows a different priority's category with no linking text.
logic.fix: Prefer the quick-win category. If you fall back, add a lead-in such as 'For your priority X'. Guard want=[] by skipping the size filter.

logic.issue: aiForProblems ranks tools purely by list order (`.slice(0,3)`). The first three in several categories are enterprise-only or off-target, which contradicts the label 'Low-cost tools you can trial in days'.
logic.scenario: p11 'no tested backup or ransomware plan' and p15 'staff use AI with no rules' both map to Cybersecurity and get Darktrace, SentinelOne Purple AI and CrowdStrike Charlotte AI, all Enterprise SOC tools that fix neither problem. p8 'onboarding and training records on paper' and p51 'staff scheduling and labour costs' map to HR & Recruiting and get Paradox (Workday, Enterprise), Eightfold (Enterprise) and Ashby ($400/mo); Education gives Khanmigo (a K-12 tutor). p1, p2 and p3 (month-end, slow invoicing, cash flow) get Stampli (AP, Custom), Ironclad (enterprise CLM) and Harvey (law-firm Enterprise), none of which handles AR, invoicing or cash forecasting. p39 'want to sell online' gets Nosto (Custom enterprise personalisation) first.
logic.fix: Change ai_prob to map problem to a curated list of tool ids (2-3 picks per problem). Failing that, rank by SME fit: free or low published tier first, drop Enterprise/Custom pricing, add an 'sme' flag. Point p15 to AI-policy guidance rather than SOC tools, and p11 to the backup/security vendor directory.

logic.issue: Coverage and ordering gaps in aiForProblems: only the first three mapped categories, in the order problems were clicked, are shown; why[c] keeps only the first problem; about 59 of 95 problems have no ai_prob mapping, so the section silently disappears (e.g., p7 payroll, p10 files on laptops, p18-p26 operations).
logic.scenario: A user picks p14 (writing) first and p2 (invoicing) third: Writing, Email and Presentation fill all three slots, and the invoicing problem gets no AI suggestion.
logic.fix: Choose one category per selected problem before taking a second from any problem, and list every problem a category answers. Add mappings, or show an explicit 'no AI tool suggested for these' note.

logic.issue: XSS through URLs: esc() HTML-escapes but doesn't check the URL scheme, so a javascript: or data: value stored in a URL field works as a live link. Fields affected: e.u (vlink in the directory and More vendors), t.u (aiCard, aiForProblems), p.url and p.src (openProd). q.c.links l[0] is inserted into href with no escaping at all (line 258). Other unescaped interpolations: e.sc in data-p (line 387), p.deploy.join (lines 325, 458), FN[x.c.fn].name (240), A.levels[].n (234), q.c.weeks (257), and x.c.id in data-goto/data-p.
logic.scenario: Tested in node: esc('javascript:alert(document.cookie)') comes back unchanged, giving <a href="javascript:alert(document.cookie)">. Any master-list row edited this way runs script when clicked. All current URLs in slices A-E start with https, so the risk is latent rather than live.
logic.fix: Add safeUrl(u) that returns u only if it matches ^https?:// (otherwise '') and use it on every href. Wrap every remaining field in esc(). Make sure the build escapes '</' (and U+2028/2029) when it writes the JSON into the #assess-data script tag. Add a CSP that blocks inline javascript: URLs.

logic.issue: The AI directory has many duplicates across categories, which inflates 'N AI tools' and lets one product take several slots. There is no status or last-verified field, so discontinued tools (Height, Clockwise, Botkeeper, Phind, Adept, Socratic, Mentat, Rewind) can't be hidden and can surface.
logic.scenario: 16 exact duplicate names (Cursor, Lovable, GitHub Copilot, Bolt.new, v0, Aider, Cline, Tabnine, etc. in both Coding/Dev and AI IDE). Notion AI appears 3 times, Synthesia 3 times and perplexity.ai 4 times.
logic.fix: Give each tool a canonical id and allow multiple categories. Add status (active, acquired, discontinued) and verified_on fields, and exclude anything not active from rendering.

logic.issue: Misleading labels. 'From our vendor directory, sized for your business' is false for unsized listings (E-L1). 'Low-cost tools you can trial in days' sits above Enterprise/Custom tools (E-L7). The AI card shows the raw pricing string, so 'Enterprise' appears under the 'low-cost' heading.
logic.scenario: Firm with fewer than 10 people that picks p11: the heading promises low-cost trials, and all three tools say 'Enterprise'.
logic.fix: Make the labels conditional, or (better) fix the selection logic. Say 'size not stated' where that applies.
